author: Marshall
asr_identification: Basārh (Muzaffarpur district): fort Rājā Bisāl kā Garh = palace
evidence: Bloch's trial excavation of the fort mound: civil centre of the 4th-5th c. AD and earlier occupation; survey of c. 12 sq. miles of the environs

author: Bloch
name_in_asr: Vaiśāli (palace; Lion pillar, Aśoka stūpa and Markaṭahrada; Saṁmatīya monastery and Licchavi relic stūpa)
asr_identification: Vaiśālī = Basarh and adjoining villages (Muzaffarpur); palace = fort Rājā Bisāl kā Garh N of Basarh; Lion pillar, stūpa and monkey tank (Rām-kund) in mauza Kollua E of Bakra, c. 2 miles NW of the fort; Saṁmatīya monastery and relic stūpa 1 mile NW of the palace, traces gone (depression E of Baniya)
evidence: survey of c. 24 sq. miles mapped exactly (Plate XXXI); fort circuit just under 5,000 ft = 4-5 li; Lion pillar 30 ft 6 in above ground; brick stūpa N of it with 12th-c. crowned Buddha (inscribed); Rām-kund 200 x 100 ft; mound reported by Mukherji at Pharawal (Ufraul) not found; Kūṭāgāra hall possibly E of Kollua
quote: The modern fort, which in its name Raja Bisal ka Garh still preserves the name of Visāla … agrees in its circumference of something less than 5,000 feet with the distance of 4 to 5 li, which Hiuen Thsang gives as the circuit of the palace of Vaisāli. … To my mind, therefore, there is no doubt that the ruins of Vaiśālī seen and described by Hiuen Thsang lay at Basarh and in its neighbourhood.
note: Same argument as Bloch's Bengal Circle report (ec1903-04, passage 555). Agrees with Mizutani (07.03 Basarh; 07.03.04 the Kolhua lion pillar) and with Cunningham (Besarh; Bakhra pillar), adding the Rām-kund as the monkey tank. Bloch could not find the relic stūpa NW of the palace (Mizutani 07.03.03 = Altekar's 1958 stūpa). Rejects some of V. A. Smith's placements (Āmrapālī's garden S of the city).; ids 07.03.02, 07.03.07 added; it is Bloch who puts Āmrapālī's garden S of the city, against Smith

author: Bloch

note: Excavation inside the fort Bloch takes for Xuanzang's palace of Vaiśālī (619); Mizutani 07.03 places the city at Basarh. The seals (625, 627) are the inscriptional evidence.
